parts.reasoning: Visual analysis indicates a standard tableware bowl likely made of glazed ceramic or porcelain, given its opaque white finish and subtle surface reflections. Assuming a typical bowl size (roughly 15cm diameter), a mass of 0.4 kg is estimated based on an average ceramic density of 2500 kg/m³. The hard, smooth glazed surface suggests moderate friction (0.4-0.5) and low restitution (0.2), as ceramic is highly inelastic and dissipates energy upon impact rather than bouncing. Crucially for simulation in Isaac Sim, the concave shape requires a 'convex_decomposition' collider to accurately model the hollow interior volume, allowing other objects to be placed inside; a simple convex hull would incorrectly enclose the top opening. Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is recommended to prevent thin-wall tunneling if small objects interact with the bowl at high velocities.
